### 2. COURSE BRIEF

### COURSE TITLE SECURITY ETHICS

### AND REGULATIONS

### IN AI

### PRE-REQUISITES NIL

### COURSE CODE 23CS201PE408 TOTALCREDITS 3

### COURSE TYPE Specialization Elective L-T-P FORMAT 2-0-2

### 3. COURSE SUMMARY

This course provides comprehensive knowledge of AI security, ethics, governance, adversarial

machine learning, MLSecOps, AI regulations, compliance frameworks, and trustworthy AI.

Students learn AI threat modeling, secure AI lifecycle management, ethical AI design,

regulatory frameworks such as the EU AI Act, NIST AI RMF, ISO/IEC 42001 & 23894, and

India’s DPDP Act 2023 through theory and laboratory exercises.

metadata.department: Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning, Computer Science and Engineering, Information Technology

chunks.text:
### 4. COURSE-SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES (CO)

At the end of the course the students will be able to

CO1: Explain AI security principles, threat landscapes, adversarial attacks, and privacy,

fairness, accountability, and transparency (FAT) concepts in AI systems.

CO2: Apply MLSecOps principles and secure AI development practices to design, deploy,

monitor, and protect AI systems throughout the machine learning lifecycle.

CO3: Analyze ethical issues, bias, explainability, accountability, and societal impacts to

promote responsible and trustworthy AI applications.

CO4: Evaluate AI governance frameworks, regulatory requirements, international standards,

compliance strategies, and auditing practices for secure, ethical, and trustworthy AI systems.

### 5. DETAILED SYLLABUS

### UNIT I : AI Threat Landscape and Vulnerabilities

1. AI Triad: Security, Ethics, and Regulation

2. AI System Lifecycle and Associated Risks

3. Privacy, Fairness, Accountability, Transparency -FAT* in AI Context

4. Evolving Threat Landscape: Adversarial AI

5. Evasion: Fooling Deployed Models, Poisoning Attacks: Corrupting Learning Process

6. Inference and Extraction Attacks: Stealing Secrets

7. LLM and Transformer Vulnerabilities: Prompt Injection and Jailbreaking

8. LLM and RAG Vulnerabilities: Data Poisoning, Supply Chain and Vector DB Issues

9. Frameworks for Understanding AI Threats: MITRE ATLAS

2. A maximum of 5% shall be allowed under medical grounds and 5% on representing the

3. Students with less than 65% of attendance shall be prevented from writing the final

assessment.

17. Academic Dishonesty & Plagiarism

Plagiarism is "to offer work or ideas from another source as one's own, with or without

authorization of the source author(s), directly by verbatim copying or by usage of any AI

software" (i.e., with or without permission from the original author). In certain cases,

authorization might be provided for the usage of other sources through written permission

may not be considered as plagiarism. It is a serious academic offence which should be

avoided, the following method will be adopted to evaluate plagiarism in submitted

documents including assignments, material, class test content and other similar academic

documents.

Level 1: Similarities up to 20% - Student will be asked to revise the document and resubmit

for evaluation, once chance will be provided to revise.

Level 2: Similarities above 20% to 40%- Student will be warned and one chance will be

provided to revise the document and resubmit.
